title: Piston mass calculation
description: Essential Criteria: Student must correctly calculate the piston mass using the hydrostatic pressure balance equation.

title: Initial gas pressure
description: Important Criteria: Student must determine the initial gas pressure by considering atmospheric pressure and the hydrostatic pressure from the water column height difference.

title: Boyle's Law application
description: Essential Criteria: Student must apply Boyle's Law correctly to find the final length of the gas column when pressures equalize.

title: Geometric height relationship
description: Important Criteria: Student must establish the correct geometric relationship between piston displacement, water level change, and gas column length change.

title: Final numerical answers
description: Essential Criteria: Student must provide both final answers with correct units: piston mass (0.10 kg) and piston rise height (10.5 cm).

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional Criteria: Student demonstrates consistent unit conversion between cm/m and cm²/m² throughout calculations.

title: Hydrostatic pressure sign error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Student incorrectly adds/subtracts hydrostatic pressure term when calculating initial gas pressure.

title: Geometric misinterpretation
description: Pitfall Criteria: Student incorrectly relates piston displacement to water level changes (e.g., forgetting the h/2 term or confusing L₂-L₁).
